title: Inter-Team Communication Protocol
purpose: Define when to use hub-and-spoke vs direct channels vs broadcast for inter-team communication, based on empirical benchmarks showing hub is 1.9x faster for single-thread coordinator ops (0.264ms median) while channels deliver 1.9x better p95 tail latency under concurrent load (55ms vs 105ms). Communication overhead is negligible (<0.05% of runtime) regardless of pattern, so the choice is about latency profile, not cost.
scope: All multi-agent operations requiring inter-team or intra-team communication. Covers coordinator-to-agent, agent-to-agent, and broadcast patterns.

hub_single_thread.best_for: Single-writer coordinator operations where one entity reads/writes and p95 <2ms is acceptable

strengths: Concurrent messaging with 8+ threads (p95 55ms vs hub 105ms)
channels_concurrent.best_for: Inter-agent messaging under concurrent load, multi-consumer broadcast, scenarios with >4 simultaneous writers

key_findings.overall_overhead: Communication overhead is 0.047% of runtime (15.9ms over 34s in live test). Pattern choice affects latency profile, not total cost.

proto_a_vs_proto_b.proto_a: 2.5% more data yield in live tests (70 vs 60 data points). 2.05 dp/s vs 2.0 baseline.
proto_a_vs_proto_b.proto_b: 82% of baseline throughput. Higher fixed cost from FIFO+mmap. Zero rate-limiter risk.
proto_a_vs_proto_b.recommendation: Use Proto A (JSONL+SQLite WAL) as default. Consider Proto B for latency-sensitive paths where rate limiter issues are a concern.

step_2a.rationale: Hub median is 0.264ms vs channels 0.492ms. 1.9x faster for single-writer ops. All coordinator dashboard, status, registration, and instruction operations should use hub.

2_to_4_writers.rationale: Hub concurrent p95 is 105ms at 10 threads. At 2-4 writers, contention is manageable.
2_to_4_writers.fallback: Switch to channels if observed p95 exceeds 50ms

5_plus_writers.rationale: At 8+ simultaneous senders, channels p95 is 55ms vs hub 105ms. Channels handle concurrent writes with 1.9x better tail latency.

step_3.question: Is this a broadcast or point-to-point?

broadcast_to_many.rationale: Progress broadcast via channels is 0.32ms. Bottleneck detection is 0.012ms. Both are faster than hub broadcast alternatives.

point_to_point.rationale: Named peer-to-peer channels avoid broadcast overhead. Channel creation is 0.32ms one-time cost.

procedures.title: Determine Communication Topology
procedures.action: Before launching teams, map out the communication needs: which teams need to talk to which, whether communication is coordinator-centric or peer-to-peer, and the expected concurrency level.
procedures.output: Communication topology diagram listing hub connections and channel connections

procedures.title: Configure Hub for Coordinator Operations
procedures.action: Set up hub-and-spoke for all coordinator functions: agent registration, status reporting, dashboard monitoring, instruction broadcast, and idle detection. The coordinator is the single writer for these operations.
procedures.output: Hub configured with coordinator as central node

procedures.title: Configure Channels for Inter-Team Messaging
procedures.action: Create direct channels for team-to-team communication, progress broadcasting, and work stealing notifications. Use topic-based channel naming for broadcast patterns.

channel_types.work_queues: Separate from messaging channels. Use WorkStealing module for queue operations.

procedures.title: Set Latency Budgets
procedures.action: Define acceptable latency thresholds for each communication path. Monitor p95 latency during operation. Escalate if thresholds are exceeded.

procedures.title: Monitor Communication Health
procedures.action: During operation, monitor communication latency via coordinator dashboard. Check for message delivery failures, rate limit denials, and bus file growth.
monitoring_checks: Channel p95 latency < 60ms under concurrent load
Message delivery rate > 96% (Proto A live test achieved 96.2%)
Bus file size < 1MB (trigger rotation if exceeded, see SOP-034)
Rate limit denial rate < 5% (64.6% denial rate is the known critical bug)
procedures.output: Communication health metrics logged per phase

small_team_3_agents.rationale: 3 agents generate minimal concurrency. Hub handles all communication with <15ms total overhead.

medium_team_5_8_agents.rationale: Hub for coordinator. Channels for inter-agent progress and work stealing. Keeps concurrent writers under the hub p95 threshold.
medium_team_5_8_agents.channels_needed: 2-4 topic channels + direct channels as needed

large_team_9_15_agents.topology: Hub + topic channels + direct channels + partitioned work queues
large_team_9_15_agents.rationale: At 9+ agents, hub concurrent p95 exceeds 100ms for inter-agent messaging. All peer communication must go through channels. Partition work queues to stay under SQLite 4-writer cliff.

multi_team_operations_14_plus.topology: Hub per coordinator + inter-team channels + team-specific topic channels
multi_team_operations_14_plus.rationale: Multiple coordinators each manage a sub-team via hub. Inter-team communication uses channels exclusively. See SOP-032 mixed operations structure.
multi_team_operations_14_plus.sqlite_partitioning: 1 hub database per sub-coordinator. Max 4 writers per database.

anti_patterns.name: Hub for Everything
anti_patterns.description: Routing all inter-agent messages through the hub under concurrent load.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: Hub p95 is 105ms with 10 concurrent threads vs channels 55ms. Hub serializes writes, creating a bottleneck.
anti_patterns.fix: Use hub only for coordinator-centric ops. Use channels for peer-to-peer under concurrency.

anti_patterns.name: Channel Sprawl
anti_patterns.description: Creating a unique channel for every possible agent pair.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: N agents = N*(N-1)/2 channels. At 15 agents that is 105 channels. Overhead from channel creation (0.32ms each) and monitoring becomes significant.
anti_patterns.fix: Use topic channels for broadcast. Create direct channels only for frequent point-to-point pairs.

anti_patterns.name: Ignoring Thundering Herd
anti_patterns.description: Having many agents poll the same work queue simultaneously without single-consumer optimization.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: 10 threads competing for 50 items adds 120x tail latency (p95: 79ms vs 0.66ms single-thread).
anti_patterns.fix: Use single-consumer work stealing when possible. Reserve multi-consumer for when p95 >80ms is acceptable.

references.data_points: Hub vs channels A/B comparison, 50+ measurements per condition

compliance_indicators: Hub used for all coordinator-centric operations
Channels used for inter-team messaging when >4 concurrent writers expected
Latency budgets defined before operation start
Communication health monitored during operation with checks every 30s
metrics.measurement_method: Log p95 latency for hub and channel operations per phase. Compare against budgets. Flag any communication path exceeding 2x its budget.
